correctness.rationale: Normalize the inner factor by making it monic and subtracting its constant, absorbing the affine change in the outer factor. Centering the composite forces the next-to-leading inner coefficient to vanish (its coefficient in the composite is the outer degree times that inner coefficient). For inner degree 2 this gives t² and the even coefficient plane. For outer degree 2 the composite is H²+bH with the stated H. Descending from a_{2m−2} to a_{m+1} gives each h_j as half a high coefficient minus an expression in already recovered h's, and a_m then gives b. Every high vector therefore occurs and uniquely determines the low vector F(x). Since m is odd, P(t)→P(−t) acts on (H,b) by (−H(−t),−b); graph uniqueness implies parity equivariance. The shear y→y−F(x) is polynomially invertible and preserves the equations for the even plane because the odd part of F vanishes on even high vectors. The two resulting ideals (u,w) and (v,w) intersect in (w,u_i v_j) and sum to (u,v,w). Fixed graph points are precisely b=0 with H odd, giving H=tW(t²). The coordinate ring is the fiber product of the two polynomial rings over the shared z-ring. Its finite integral closure is their product; multiplying by the component idempotents shows that the conductor consists exactly of pairs with both restrictions zero. Off the intersection there is one regular branch; on it there are two local minimal primes. Translation at any closed intersection point followed by completion gives the stated formal monomial ring. Counting monomials in two 2d-variable rings with their d-variable overlap subtracted proves the series, dimension, embedding dimension and multiplicity. In the fiber-product exact sequence, the middle and last depths are 2d and d; local cohomology vanishes below d+1 for the first term and is nonzero in degree d+1. For prime p≥5 the invariant-Bezoutian criterion in the cited Theorem 5.3 applies in composite degree 2p, with exactly the two listed factorizations and no prime-degree Dickson exception. Non-Cohen–Macaulayness on the intersection also holds at nonclosed points by the same depth argument after localizing along the shared z-plane.

value.rationale: A global affine description of the union of the natural two competing composition types determines the conductor, tangent size, scheme gluing and uniform depth defect along the intersection. The failure of Cohen–Macaulayness for the full reduced prime-index locus persists despite the smoothness of each component and their reduced intersection. This answers a structural question about the reducibility locus, beyond the known embedding of each branch or an isolated low-degree computation.
residual_risks: No inference is made about nonreduced or projective scheme structures.
